round_a.question: v2 (editorial lab) vs v1 (plain): scores, beat ranking, 3D, dark, build log
round_a.brief:
PRODUCT (unchanged from round 1): "Pill" — Cal Hacks 13.0 team project. A $40 lab-in-a-box (ESP32 + LEDs + 2 light sensors + thermistor + stirring paddle, in a dark chamber) that dissolves one tablet and tells you PASS / NEEDS LAB / UNABLE TO VERIFY, plus a bottle-photo recall check. Clinic mode gates the supplier's payment in a Capital One Nessie SANDBOX (released only on PASS and a human tap; NEEDS LAB holds; UNABLE TO VERIFY escalates). Personal mode keeps a "My medicines" list. Built on Peel (HackMIT 2026 grand prize, MIT licence, cited openly). One calibrated reference drug only: riboflavin (vitamin B2). Every other pill returns UNABLE TO VERIFY by design. The station chamber is being 3D-printed Saturday from a CAD file the team made, so the CAD already exists.
VERIFIED FACTS: WHO 2017: "1 in 10 medical products in developing countries is substandard or falsified". LSHTM model cited by WHO: 116,000 (64,000-158,000) additional malaria deaths a year in sub-Saharan Africa from substandard AND falsified antimalarials (an estimate). Everything else about results (plateau numbers, N runs, "first PASS at 13:00") is PLANNED, not yet measured — the timeline in beat 9 is the plan, not history.
JUDGING: main criteria Application, Intentionality, Functionality, Creativity, Technical complexity. Judges: 5 min per table, ~700 projects. Sponsors read Devpost asynchronously. Figma "Best Design" is judged on workflow design, adoptability, output quality, pitch, innovation and requires a stage log + Figma Slides. Submission Sun 8:30 AM.

ROUND 1 (yesterday, you were on that panel): the 16 personas scored "copy an Apple/Oura-style storytelling site" 3.7/10 and "plain, fast, honest page" 8.0/10, unanimously picked "real device photo + one line" as the opener, and produced an 8-section outline (hero / problem / how it works / real results + clip / clinic payment gate / personal mode / honest limits / built on Peel + team). Top do-not-do list: no "safe/verified/authentic/certified", no unsourced stats or live counters, no mockups in place of real curves and screenshots, no scroll-jacking/pinned sections/heavy WebGL/slow load (<2 MB, Lighthouse ≥80, 3G), don't blur what is new vs Peel, no stock photos, no renders or AI images of the device, no vague payment gate, no accuracy claims without N, show the non-happy paths.

V1 = the round-1 plain page: 8 sections, one student, ~8 h Saturday, CSS fade-in only, phone photos, one real curve chart, one clip, ≤2 MB.

V2 = the new plan ("editorial lab", written after Preston asked for a premium page with a 3D orientation of the device and a visible story, timeline and problems). It keeps every round-1 honesty rule and adds:
- Direction: "editorial lab, not SaaS template" — Teenage Engineering / lab-notebook voice, big quiet type (Satoshi 56-88 px headings, JetBrains Mono for numbers/run ids/rule ids), paper #F6F5F2 / ink #101214, one accent (LED blue #2F6BFF) for links, curve and hotspots; verdict green/amber/grey, no red. 12-col grid, 1200 px max, 96-144 px section padding, figure captions "Fig 1." in mono, 8-px rhythm, hairline rules, favicon, OG image, printable Report page.
- OPTIONAL DARK VARIANT (#0B0C0E background, paper text) for sections 3-6 only (3D model, physics, scan curve, verdict cards) "so the 3D and the curve sit on black like the inside of the chamber: the one dramatic move". Sections 1-2 and 7-10 stay paper.
- 3D: the real station's CAD exported to GLB, loaded with <model-viewer> (Apache-2.0, one tag), 6 hotspots, exploded-view toggle (second GLB), poster image for first paint, lazy-loaded, ≤3 MB. Plan allots roughly 3 h total (export + hotspots + integration) across the design and build tracks. If the GLB is late, beat 3 ships with an exploded photo instead.
- Data as art: every chart is real data from the box with a run id under it; 2 charts (the B2-vs-Tums curve; the 15-run calibration overview).
- Length: 10 sections, ~9 desktop screens (~8,000 px at 1440×900), ~15 mobile screens, 550-700 words, 10-12 real photos, 1 GLB, 1 clip (90 s, click-to-play, captioned, ≤15 MB), ≤6 MB first load incl. GLB poster-first, Lighthouse mobile ≥85, prefers-reduced-motion disables every animation. Target: a judge gets the story from the first 3 screens in 60 s; 3 min for all.
- Motion: fade-up on entry, SVG stroke draw, number count-up once, 80 ms card stagger, slow model auto-rotate. Nothing pinned, no scroll-jacking, no parallax.
- Build-log beat (9): a horizontal timeline of the 36 hours with phone photos and timestamps, plus a "What broke" list of 3-5 honest bullets and what was done.
- Still not doing: pinned Three.js scrub, live death counter, autoplay hero, renders of imagined hardware, stock photos, AI images, the words safe/verified/authentic/certified/guaranteed/AI-powered, purple gradients.
- STAFFING CHANGE: v2 is TWO people on Saturday (one design/content in Figma ~10 h, one build ~11 h), with hardware and app teams delivering assets at 13:00, 15:00 and 17:00. v1 was one student, 8 h. The team is 3-4 people total and the hardware (10-20 B2 calibration runs, the print, the Nessie flow) is being built the same day.
